brief: Implied vol fell across asset classes last week after the Fed hiked rates 25bps as expected, with rate vol (MOVE), oil vol (OVX) and equity vol (VIX) all lower; FX and credit screen cheapest on a 10-year lookback while gold and oil screen richest. Single-stock vol diverged from index vol: VIXEQ rose even as VIX fell, widening the VIX-VIXEQ spread and pushing the DSPX dispersion index up off its recent low. Options positioning turned more constructive, with SPX skew flattening as investors sold hedges and rotated into calls, lifting SPX call skew. Equity correlations stayed muted overall, but cross-asset correlations grew more extreme: equity-rates correlation has stayed negative since the Iran War began, equity-oil correlation is near an extreme negative, and the 3-month oil/10Y Treasury yield correlation hit +65%, a 35-year high just below the 1990 Gulf War record of 66%. If the pattern holds, the note argues yields will depend more on Iran than the Fed.
